typical_symptoms: Appearance of small angular light-green to pale yellow spots on the upper leaf surface
Development of a powdery white to greyish fungal growth on the underside of leaves
Premature senescence, drying, and heavy defoliation of lower mature leaves
Coalescence of angular spots into larger brown necrotic areas
visual_characteristics: Distinctly geometric, angular leaf lesions defined strictly by fine leaf veinlets
Frosty or velvety greyish-white conidial mats restricted to the abaxial leaf surface
Translucent pale yellow angular patches visible from the adaxial leaf surface
lesion_characteristics: Strictly angular, polygonal shape defined by small veinlets
Well-defined sharp margins following leaf architecture
Individual spots 1 to 4 mm in size, frequently coalescing into larger patches
Slight yellow border initially, progressing to complete tissue necrosis
color_characteristics: Starts as pale green or yellowish-green translucent spots
White to pale grey sporulation layer on the lower surface
Matures to tan, dull brown, or dark brown necrotic spots before leaf drop
spatial_patterns: Scattered predominantly across mature canopy leaves
Spreading upwards from the lower canopy to upper leaves in humid conditions
distinguishing_features: Geometric angular shape strictly bounded by veinlets, creating a mosaic-like pattern
Greyish-white powdery sporulation strictly restricted within the boundaries of the angular lesions on the lower leaf surface
